papers.title: Analysis of Microhardness after Turning Process of Ti6Al4V-ELI
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effect of cutting parameters on the microhardness of Ti6Al4V ELI during dry turning using PVD AlTiN and TiAlN inserts. Addressing the challenge of balancing productivity with stringent surface integrity requirements, this research explored the influence of cutting speed (80, 125, and 170 m/min) and feed rate (0.08, 0.15, and 0.20 mm/rev) on subsurface microhardness. Vickers microhardness testing revealed a clear work hardening tendency, with the highest microhardness observed in the subsurface region. Increasing cutting speed correlated with increased microhardness, particularly when using PVD TiAlN inserts, indicating a greater degree of microstructural alteration. A thicker white layer was observed after turning with PVD AlTiN inserts compared to PVD TiAlN, potentially due to differences in friction coefficient. Maximum microhardness (398 HV0.05) was recorded at 125 m/min cutting speed and 0.20 mm/rev feed rate with PVD TiAlN. The machining affected zone (MAZ) extended to 200 µm and 300 µm below the surface for AlTiN and TiAlN inserts, respectively. These findings provide insights for optimizing machining processes to enhance both surface integrity and productivity in the manufacturing of Ti6Al4V ELI components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是常规锻造Ti6Al4V-ELI的车削加工，未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理，与用户方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper investigates turning of wrought Ti6Al4V-ELI, not additive-manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it does not address any post-processing treatment specific to AM material.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of cutting parameters on subsurface microhardness of Ti6Al4V ELI during dry turning.
summary_en.method: Turning experiments with PVD AlTiN and TiAlN inserts at various cutting speeds and feed rates, followed by Vickers microhardness testing.
summary_en.result: Higher cutting speed increased microhardness, with maximum hardness of 398 HV0.05 at 125 m/min and 0.20 mm/rev using TiAlN inserts.
summary_en.validation: Experimental microhardness measurements confirmed work hardening and machining affected zone depths.

papers.title: The critical role of optimized energy density in controlling void morphology and enhancing mechanical properties of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI alloy
papers.abstract: Laser power is referred to as one of the critical process parameters governing the volumetric energy density in the Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF) process. The purpose of the study is to systematically investigate the influence of laser energy density on the void morphology, microstructure, and mechanical properties of the L-PBF printed parts which were fabricated with laser power ranging from 75 to 175 W. Comprehensive analysis of void defect was conducted by employing Archimedes' method, optical microscope (OM), and X-ray microcomputed tomography (Micro-CT). Surface quality was analyzed by surface roughness measurement. Tensile testing was performed to establish the correlation between process parameters, material microstructure, and mechanical behavior in as-built samples. Under the optimal process parameters, this work achieved a minimum void fraction of 0.3%. At various laser energy densities, three distinct morphologies, namely lack of fusion (LOF), gas pores (GP), and keyhole (KH), were generated. Notably, LOF has a more detrimental effect on tensile characteristics, in comparison to GP and KH defects if laser power was less than 100 W. Interestingly, subsurface spherical pores at the hatch border demonstrate a less substantial influence on the tensile behavior of as-built samples than LOF. The correlation analysis revealed that the presence of void defects primarily influenced strength, modulus of elasticity, and strain at break. Energy density proved to play a pivotal role in defect generation, non-equilibrium microstructure, and mechanical properties of L-PBF. Based on our findings, selecting 100 W of laser power with a speed of 1200 mm/sec could be an optimal choice for achieving a satisfactory result in as-built L-PBF part.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接针对L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI合金的工艺参数-孔隙-力学性能关系，完全符合L1层对Ti-6Al-4V增材制造力学性能的关注。
llm.why_not_core: No fatigue or cyclic loading data; only quasi-static tensile properties are reported.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究激光能量密度对L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI合金孔隙形态和力学性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 改变激光功率（75-175 W），利用Archimedes法、OM和Micro-CT分析孔隙，并进行拉伸测试。
summary_zh.result: 最优参数下孔隙率0.3%，未熔合缺陷比气孔和匙孔对拉伸性能影响更大。
summary_zh.validation: 通过Archimedes法、光学显微镜、Micro-CT和拉伸测试进行实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To systematically investigate the effect of laser energy density on void morphology, microstructure, and mechanical properties of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V ELI alloy.
summary_en.method: Samples fabricated with laser power from 75 to 175 W were analyzed using Archimedes method, optical microscopy, micro-CT, surface roughness measurement, and tensile testing.
summary_en.result: Optimal parameters yielded 0.3% porosity, with lack-of-fusion defects more detrimental than gas pores or keyhole pores, and energy density critically influencing defect generation and tensile properties.
summary_en.validation: Experimental characterization via Archimedes method, OM, Micro-CT, and tensile testing.
